blocks.content: I walk when I'm looking for something to paint. No destination, no plan — just moving until something stops me. Every time I've tried to plan a painting in advance, the planned version turns out worse than whatever I would have found if I'd just walked.
My middle school art teacher called it wandering with intention. My mother calls it refusing to commit. They're both right.

It was past nine and the town had done its morning transformation — the quiet version of itself replaced by the version with traffic and open storefronts and people who weren't just somewhere but actually somewhere. I kept to the back streets.

There's an alley on Clement with a mural I've been circling for a month. Someone painted it years ago, festival project probably, and the color has gone thin in places, but the composition is still good — a figure reaching for something just out of frame, real ivy climbing the left border into painted ivy, the line between art and wall and art again going soft. I stop there most mornings. I've never set up there. It always feels like it's waiting for something I haven't figured out yet.
I stopped now and looked at it.
For no particular reason, my mind went back to the tilt of her head as she stepped off the bus. The way the silver bracelet caught the light.
I redirected. I looked at the mural. I thought about the mural. I'm a professional.
